jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Economics and Business at Colorado College
jobs.description: Employer: Colorado College Expires: 10/14/2026 Assistant Professor of Economics and Business To apply, please visit: https://apptrkr.com/7330126 Job Title: Assistant Professor of Economics and Business Position Status: Tenure-Track Academic Rank: Assistant Professor Department: Economics and Business Campus Location: Main Campus Job Summary The Department of Economics and Business at Colorado College invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Economics and Business with specialization in marketing, to begin Fall 2027. The department offers four undergraduate degrees which reflect our interdisciplinary approach to economics and business: (1) Business, Economics, and Society; (2) Economics; (3) International Political Economy; and (4) Mathematical Economics. We engage students in immersive pedagogy via field trips, community-engaged work, and intensive group projects. Responsibilities for this position entail teaching five courses annually plus advising students' senior theses, which counts as a sixth course. Faculty are also expected to maintain an active research program and engage in college service. A successful candidate will have: • A PhD in Business or related fields (ABD candidates will also be considered) • Excellent teaching promise • The ability to teach Consumer Marketing (https://coursecatalog.coloradocollege.edu/courses/BU326) and other marketing courses • Willingness and ability to teach two courses annually in the broader departmental and general education curriculum as assigned, such as Introduction to Business and Society (https://coursecatalog.coloradocollege.edu/courses/BU201), Principles of Financial Accounting (https://coursecatalog.coloradocollege.edu/courses/BU205), Society, Business, and Economics (https://coursecatalog.coloradocollege.edu/courses/BU310), Business Analytics (https://coursecatalog.coloradocollege.edu/courses/BU318), Qualitative Research Methods (https://coursecatalog.coloradocollege.edu/courses/BU319), First-Year Critical Inquiry Seminar (https://coursecatalog.coloradocollege.edu/courses/CC100), or First-Year Writing Seminar (https://coursecatalog.coloradocollege.edu/courses/CC120). No experience with such courses is required, only willingness to learn • An active research agenda aimed at peer-reviewed publications commensurate with selective liberal arts institutions (for reference, faculty cvs are https://www.coloradocollege.edu/academics/dept/economics/people/department-faculty.html; college requirements for tenure are found https://www.coloradocollege.edu/offices/humanresources/people-practices/handbooks/facultyhandbook.pdf on pp. 16-18; the department statement on scholarship is found https://cctigers-my.sharepoint.com/:b:/g/personal/crader_coloradocollege_edu/EemhqXVZkJ9OrEmBcQLmp0gBC04KyT7NpsaVspa7VxB0QA?e=8ScNfa.) Colorado College is a nationally recognized, residential liberal arts and sciences college enrolling approximately 2,100 students from across the US and around the world. The College, located on a 99-acre campus in Colorado Springs, is distinguished by its immersive learning and pedagogy made possible by the Block Plan, in which professors teach, and students take, one course at a time. Each block is three and a half weeks long, allowing for unique teaching and learning strategies. Professors have a six-block teaching duty in the eight-block year, where one of the six blocks may be assigned to supervising senior and independent projects where the work is spread out across the year rather than completed in a conventional block. Colorado College actively promotes a dynamic and inclusive environment in which students and employees of diverse backgrounds, cultures, and perspectives can learn and work. Read more about our the College's commitment in our https://www.coloradocollege.edu/offices/adei/ and the strategic plan "https://www.coloradocollege.edu/offices/adei/strategic-plan.html." Minimum Qualifications Ph.D. or DBA in Business or related field by the start of employment plus research in marketing. A Ph.D. in Psychology, Economics, Statistics, or Sociology or a JD may be considered provided it is accompanied by academic research in marketing and experience teaching marketing. Preferred Qualifications Undergraduate teaching experience Application Instructions • Continuous Recruitment - This position may close without notice. For full consideration, apply by: 07-01-2026• References will be contacted to upload a letter of recommendation when a candidate accepts a Zoom/Phone interview• For any questions, contact the chair of the search committee, Dr. Christina Rader, mailto:crader@coloradocollege.edu. You must meet the minimum qualifications to be considered for this position. Required Documents Applicants should submit 1) a cover letter; 2) a curriculum vitae; 3) a teaching statement; 4) evidence of teaching ability such as course evaluations and syllabi; 5) a research statement (3 pages maximum); 6) sample of research; 7) undergraduate and graduate transcripts (unofficial copies and screenshots are suitable for applications; the successful candidate will be required to send official transcripts); and 8) contact information for three references. Optional Documents -- Anticipated Hiring Salary Range: https://www.coloradocollege.edu/offices/humanresources/employee-compensation/ Visa Sponsorship Information: Eligible for H-1B sponsorship contingent on being eligible for exemption and/or exception of the $100,000.00 petition fee What We Offer: As part of the total compensation for Staff and Faculty roles, we offer a competitive benefits package including: -Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance-Retirement plan (403b) where CC contributes 10%, with a mandated 5% employee contribution-Paid seasonal breaks and holidays (20 days per year)-Tuition assistance benefits for employee and their eligible dependents-Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) Assistance Program-Wellness benefits including free access to the fitness center, swimming pool, wellness center, and financial consultants Benefits and Wellness Information: Please refer to our https://www.coloradocollege.edu/offices/humanresources/benefits/index.html Accommodation Statement: In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, and Colorado College's policies, if you have a disability and would like to request accommodations to support your application or interview process, please contact Human Resources at mailto:HR@coloradocollege.edu as early as possible. For more information, visit http://www.e-verify.gov Leave Information: Please refer to https://www.coloradocollege.edu/basics/welcome/leadership/policies/vacation-leave-and-accrual.html EOE Statement: Colorado College is committed to equal opportunity for all employees and applicants in all aspects of the employment relationship-including (but not limited to) recruiting, hiring, promotions, compensation, benefits, and access to training-without regard to race, creed, color, caste, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity or gender expression, perceived gender, sexual preferences and sexual orientation), disability, marital status, veteran status, age, genetic information, or any other status protected by federal, state, or local law. jobs.title: Associate Vice President of Healthy Living at YMCA of the Triangle
jobs.description: Employer: YMCA of the Triangle Expires: 10/14/2026 POSITION SUMMARY: Under the supervision of the Vice President of Operations and Healthy Living and in cooperation with YMCA staff, the Associate VP of Healthy Living ensures branches deliver a safe and high-quality member experience that is designed to meet the unique member programming and health and well-being goals of participants that the Y of the Triangle serves. The candidate must be able to apply critical thinking abilities and utilize effective communication skills to develop strategic plans and effective messages to support the YMCA of the Triangle’s Healthy Living efforts. The AVP of Healthy Living will partner with Branch Membership and Healthy Living Departments across the Association to develop curriculum and deliver engaging, high quality and consistent wellness programs that increase member engagement, retention and growth of revenue. The incumbent will also focus on connecting members to small membership/wellness/fitness communities within our Y. They will be responsible for managing such functions in accordance with the stated mission and polices established by the administrative staff, governing committees and Board of Directors of the YMCA. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: Strategy, Programs & Growth Provides vision and leadership for the YMCA of the Triangle’s Membership Experience. Accountable for program design implementation for existing and future program models and ensuring program fidelity. Responsible for developing, leading and supporting the YMCA of the Triangle’s Membership and Wellness/Fitness Programs – focusing on group fitness, personal/small group training and member onboarding – in collaboration and partnership with Membership, Healthy Living Directors, ARC and branch leadership. Leads innovation, collaboration and program integration among Membership, Wellness, Personal Training and Group Fitness Programs. Responsible for developing, leading and supporting the YMCA of the Triangle’s Personal Training and Small Group Training Program in collaboration and partnership with Healthy Living Directors and branch leadership. Responsibility for leading efforts with Healthy Living Directors and branch leadership to grow revenue of Personal Training/Small Group programs Leads the planning, project management and execution of association-wide program launches, service enhancements, curriculum updates and strategic initiatives, ensuring projects are delivered on time, within scope and aligned with organizational goals. Serves as executive sponsor and project leader for enterprise Healthy Living and Membership initiatives, coordinating cross-functional teams, resources, timelines, communications and implementation plans across the Association. Research, report and make decisions based on analytics of the latest trends and development in the membership and fitness industry. Operations, Performance & Continuous Improvement Monitors and tracks all data related to membership and wellness programs across the association. Develops strategies to close gaps identified in relevant data related to the various program areas: Membership, Group Fitness, Personal Training/Small Group Training and Equipment. Explores ways, through data-driven decisions, to enhance and promote the quality of the association’s membership and wellness programs with a focus on membership growth and retention. Monitors and tracks all data related to group fitness, personal training and small group training across the association including branch reservations systems, participation numbers and quality/experience of class participants – to inform schedules, offerings and growth opportunities. Works in collaboration with IT to create tools in PowerBI. Develops project charters, implementation plans, success metrics and stakeholder communication strategies for major operational and strategic initiatives. Works with Branch and Association Operation teams to evaluate group wellness/fitness environments (i.e. studio lighting, sound systems, supplemental equipment, stage, flooring and color schemes) and makes recommendations to enhance the experience/program. People Leadership, Training & Team Development Supervises, coaches and leads the Healthy Living/Membership Experience team comprised of Association Director of Member Experience, Association Director of Wellness Experience and Association Equipment Coordinator. Leads the collaboration with the Association Director of Community Health and the Association Director of Membership Experience and Association Director Wellness Experience to: Support the innovation, pathway, engagement and onboarding of members to group wellness programs. Support the pathway, engagement and onboarding of members into Community health programs. Support all members in their journey to reach their health and wellness goals. Works collaboratively with the Operational Vice Presidents, ARC Department Heads, Employee Resource Groups and Branch leadership to: Provide on-going leadership and direction to membership and wellness professionals Ensure consistent on-boarding for new membership, wellness and group fitness full-time directors and staff Ensure program quality, standards and expectations in related areas that meet the needs of our existing membership in supporting their health and well-being goals Provides leadership and supports the work of the Membership (Membership Directors) and Wellness Teams (Healthy Living Directors) at branches and other cross-departmental teams related to member experience. Leads and facilitates cross-functional project teams, steering committees and workgroups, ensuring accountability, alignment and successful execution of strategic priorities. Supports recruitment and selection of wellness staff across multiple dimensions of diversity, supporting branches to acquire and develop high-quality Adult Associates, Healthy Living Directors, group fitness instructors, personal trainers and wellness coaches. Actively audits classes and programs for quality, instructor coaching opportunities and curriculum delivery - working during branch peak hours, which include mornings, evenings and weekends. Supports the Association’s Quarterly Launch for new Group Wellness/Fitness Programs. This includes branch team practices, tracking allocations and supporting all education/curriculum efforts of new program materials for the Y. Designs and leads an onboarding system for wellness, personal training and group fitness for current and new YMCA members. Provides strategic oversight and project governance for the Personal Training and Small Group Training portfolio, including planning, implementation, evaluation and continuous improvement efforts. Partnerships, Resources & Communication Leads enterprise equipment planning and capital projects, including needs assessment, budgeting, vendor coordination, implementation planning, stakeholder communication and project execution. Works collaboratively with the CFO, COO, VP of Finance, VP of Healthy Living creating the annual equipment budget. In partnership with the Association Equipment Coordinator, leads wellness floor design and fitness equipment asset management. Negotiates contracts, builds and maintains relationships with equipment vendors who supply products and services for wellness, personal training and group fitness programs. Leads the Personal Training and Small Group Training Project Team. Leads and directs the implementation and ongoing integration of fitness engagement technology platforms, including Fisikal, NetGym, Myzone and Evolt, while supporting the strategic vision and direction of the YMCA mobile app. Ensures brand compliance within Association standards through marketing and communication efforts. Works in partnership with marketing & communications department to create tailored marketing collateral for membership/group wellness/fitness/exercise for both internal and external audiences. Maintains regular, clear and concise communication within area of responsibility. Models relationship-building and engagement skills in all wellness/membership interactions Develops and maintains collaborative relationships with branch leadership, membership teams and healthy living staff. Assists with Annual Campaign, as assigned. Completion of all required annual trainings related to safety, compliance and child protection as assigned. Responsible for other opportunities as assigned by VP of Operations and Healthy Living and the Association. QUALIFICATIONS: Bachelor’s degree in business, organizational development, fitness, kinesiology or a related field is required; advanced degree or equivalent experience is a plus. 8+ years of progressively responsible senior leadership experience in a membership-based organization, sales, or customer service industry. Demonstrated success leading large-scale, cross-functional projects and strategic initiatives from planning through implementation, including management of timelines, resources, budgets, stakeholders and organizational change. Proven success leading complex program, policy, technology and operational initiatives, including project planning, implementation, change management and organizational adoption. Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of the current membership and fitness industry trends, corporate wellness program development and sales strategies. Strong project management, organizational planning and execution skills with the ability to simultaneously manage multiple priorities, deadlines and stakeholders. Discipline-specific licensures and/or certifications are required. Candidates must possess a nationally recognized certification in either Group Fitness (e.g., AFAA, ACE, Les Mills) or Personal Training upon hire and must obtain certification in the other discipline within an agreed upon timeline of employment. Ability to effectively teach and model best practices in both Group Fitness and Personal Training environments is required. Hold or be willing to obtain Basic Life Support, Basic First Aid and Emergency Oxygen within the first 30 days of employment. Experience in a non-profit setting is preferred. Cultivates and actively promotes caring, honesty, respect and responsibility in all interactions. Solid business acumen and a strategic mindset, with a keen understanding of business imperatives and organizational priorities. Demonstrated ability to develop, implement and manage complex budgets, evaluate financial performance and pricing models and take proactive, decisive action to drive results and ensure financial sustainability. Proven ability to develop, lead and motivate staff, volunteers and cross-functional teams while fostering a collaborative and engaging work environment. Excellent organizational, project and time management and communication skills—both written and verbal—including the ability to deliver compelling presentations and engage audiences in person and through virtual platforms. Strong leadership, project governance and stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence and align senior leaders, branch teams, vendors and cross-functional partners toward successful project outcomes. WORK ENVIRONMENT & PHYSICAL DEMANDS: The work environment and physical demands described here represent those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Primarily office setting with occasional interaction in gyms, classrooms and outdoor spaces. Moderate noise levels; may be louder during youth or community activities. Regular use of computer, phone and other office technology for extended periods of time. Frequent sitting, standing, walking, bending and reaching; occasional lifting or moving up to 40 lbs. Must reside in the greater Triangle area of North Carolina (Raleigh-Durham-Chapel Hill and surrounding areas). Must be able to provide valid identification for employment eligibility verification. Must possess a valid driver’s license and have access to reliable transportation. A clean driving record is required to meet YMCA insurance standards. Travel between branch and/or site locations and to off-site meetings and events is required. This position is 100% in person, with the flexibility to work at various branches and program locations across the YMCA of the Triangle as needed. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential job functions. Salary & BenefitsThis is a full-time exempt position with a salary starting at $92,000, commensurate with experience and qualifications. The YMCA of the Triangle offers a generous benefits package including medical, dental and vision insurance; paid time off; an annual YMCA membership; and participation in the YMCA Retirement Fund, including a 12% employer contribution once eligibility requirements are met.

jobs.feedName: Michael D. Eisner College of Education
jobs.title: Program Associate, AmeriCorps Workforce Development at National Council on Aging
jobs.description: Employer: National Council on Aging Expires: 10/14/2026 Join Our Mission. Shape the Future. At NCOA, we are on a mission to create the conditions for all to age well in America—today and into the future. Every day, we work to improve the lives of millions of older adults through innovative programs, trusted advocacy, and meaningful partnerships that advance health, economic security, and equity. We are seeking a dynamic and collaborative Program Associate, AmeriCorps Workforce Development to bring their expertise, passion, and commitment to help drive our mission forward. This team member will play a pivotal role in supporting the AmeriCorps Seniors Workforce Development Senior Demonstration Program by coordinating participant services, strengthening community and employer partnerships, and helping older adults build the skills and experience needed to pursue meaningful employment opportunities. The ideal candidate is an organized and relationship-focused program professional who thrives on supporting participants, building community relationships, and coordinating multiple priorities to help older adults successfully navigate training, volunteer service, and pathways to employment. They will embrace and exemplify NCOA's core values of Caring for All, Collaboration, Innovation, Integrity, and Respect, fostering a culture of excellence while helping ensure that every older adult has the opportunity to age with dignity, purpose, and security. If you are ready to make a lasting difference while leading with purpose, we invite you to join our team. POSITION SUMMARY The Program Associate, AmeriCorps Workforce Development plays a key role in supporting the planning, coordination, and implementation of workforce development initiatives within the Center for Economic Well-Being (CEW). This includes providing program, participant, and operational support for the AmeriCorps Seniors Workforce Development Senior Demonstration Program (SDP) activities in Wheeling, West Virginia. Working both independently and collaboratively, the Program Associate partners with internal staff, community organizations, employers, training providers, and volunteers to support successful program implementation and advance workforce development goals. Working closely with the AmeriCorps program team, the Program Associate supports AmeriCorps Seniors volunteers throughout the West Virginia Northern Panhandle, western Pennsylvania, and eastern Ohio by coordinating participant recruitment, volunteer service, training, mentoring, and employment readiness activities for adults age 55 and older. The Program Associate builds relationships with the local business community to expand workforce opportunities for older adults and support participants in obtaining permanent employment. This position emphasizes providing quality volunteer experiences and specialized training that prepare older adults for permanent employment. About the AmeriCorps Seniors Workforce Development Senior Demonstration Program (SDP): The AmeriCorps Seniors Workforce Development Senior Demonstration Program (SDP) is funded by AmeriCorps Seniors and supports older adults in obtaining permanent employment in skilled labor and professional careers. Grantee organizations—including NCOA—provide: Training and/or certification for employment, and support such as mentorship, coaching, transportation, and other forms of support. Mentoring and/or coaching in regular increments, including during pre- and post-employment placement. A competitive stipend to remove barriers for older adults’ service. Positions at this level typically report to an associate director or director and require experience supporting projects and managing tasks or deliverables. Incumbents are required to exercise judgement within their scope of work based on defined guidelines. Incumbents generally have one or more years of experience in their discipline and a bachelor’s degree or the equivalent, as well as substantive experience at this level. Graduate level degrees may be considered in lieu of experience. *This grant-funded position is a short-term, temporary position that is funded through June 30, 2028, and designed to be filled by a W-2 employee. KEY RESPONSIBILITIESCoordinate day-to-day implementation of the AmeriCorps Seniors Workforce Development Senior Demonstration Program (SDP) to support participant success and achievement of grant objectives.Serve as a case manager for enrolled AmeriCorps Seniors volunteers to provide a path to successful program completion. This includes:Recruiting volunteers and matching them to the appropriate volunteer station.Ensuring accurate data collection and entry into the database.Conducting weekly check-ins with AmeriCorps volunteers.Supporting volunteers who need additional digital literacy training by providing them access to standard curriculum. Enrolling volunteers in appropriate specialized training courses and coordinating any certification testing needed to support their employment objectives.Identifying job opportunities for AmeriCorps Seniors volunteers who have completed their training, curriculum, and volunteer service experience and supporting their transition to permanent employment.Maintaining contact with volunteers who have exited the program to follow up on and track their employment status and income.Support the development and implementation of participant recruitment strategies to maintain consistent enrollment levels and a pipeline of prospective volunteers.Identify appropriate volunteer training sites and maintain communication with partner organizations to support positive training and volunteer experiences for AmeriCorps Seniors volunteers. Work with volunteer station partners to identify service opportunities that meet organizational needs while supporting volunteers’ employment and training goals, including opportunities for job shadowing and skill development. Customize volunteer opportunities to meet the employment training needs of each volunteer and create an individualized training plan for each volunteer. Monitor assigned program activities, participant data, and progress toward performance measures to support quality service delivery, achievement of grant objectives, and compliance with applicable grant and program requirements.Collaborate regularly in-office with other AmeriCorps Workforce Development and Program Evaluation team members to coordinate program activities, share information, and support successful grant implementation.Maintain confidentiality and comply with all applicable AmeriCorps and NCOA program standards, procedures, and data security requirements. Serve as an ambassador for NCOA’s mission, programs, and social impact goals by building and maintaining positive relationships with employers, community organizations, public and private agencies, and other external stakeholders to promote awareness of AmeriCorps Seniors, workforce development initiatives, and older worker issues.Participate in team meetings, work planning, trainings, community events, performance monitoring, and continuous improvement activities to support program and departmental goals.Conduct site visits, attend conferences and community events, participate in partner meetings, and engage in other business travel as needed to support participant services, partner relationships, program implementation, and organizational priorities.Complete required annual National Service Criminal History Check (NSCHC) training and other trainings as required by AmeriCorps and NCOA. Perform other responsibilities as assigned. PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE/QUALIFICATIONSBachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.1-3 years of relevant experience in program coordination, program support, or a similar role required; experience in workforce development, employment and training, human services, job readiness, or a related field preferred.Demonstrated ability to coordinate projects, manage multiple priorities, and meet deadlines while maintaining strong organizational skills and attention to detail.Strong verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to build effective relationships with participants, employers, community organizations, and other stakeholders.Ability to provide participant-centered case management and support, maintain ongoing participant engagement and follow-up, and respond effectively to individual participant needs.Experience supporting nonprofit or grant-funded programs, including tracking deliverables, organizing reports, monitoring activities, and assisting with day-to-day program operations, preferred.Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and experience learning and utilizing web-based data management systems, such as Salesforce or similar platforms. Demonstrated ability to work independently while contributing effectively within a collaborative, cross-functional team environment. Experience working with older adults, diverse communities, minority populations, low-income communities, or other underserved populations strongly preferred. Familiarity with workforce development resources and employer networks in the Northern Panhandle of West Virginia, eastern Ohio, or western Pennsylvania, including experience networking with public agencies and community organizations at the local level, preferred. Ability and willingness to travel regularly throughout the service area to volunteer stations, partner sites, and community locations as needed, including occasional same-day or time-sensitive travel. PHYSICAL DEMANDS The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Frequently required to sit or use a standing desk. Occasionally required to walk. Occasionally required to reach with hands and arms. Frequently required to talk or listen. jobs.description: Employer: Cincinnati Tennis Foundation Expires: 10/14/2026 Job Title: Schools & Community Educator Organization: Cincinnati Tennis Foundation Position Type: Full-Time, Hourly (Approx. 40 hours/week) Compensation: $22.00 – $26.50 / hour ($45,000 – $55,000 annualized equivalent) + seasonal overtime opportunities at $40/hr Reports To: Executive Director About Cincinnati Tennis FoundationThe Cincinnati Tennis Foundation (CTF) is a nationally recognized leader in sports-based youth development, using tennis as a vehicle for education, mentorship, and community empowerment. At its core, CTF brings physical activity and academic enrichment directly to where kids need it most by partnering with hundreds of local schools to offer accessible, in-school, and after-school programming. Beyond the court, CTF provides robust academic tutoring, college guidance, and financial resources to ensure every child has a path to success regardless of background. Operating as the primary programming partner at the world-class Cincinnati Open campus, along with expanding into a brand-new Norwood facility, CTF offers a ground-floor opportunity to shape the future of a rapidly growing, mission-driven organization.Position SummaryThe Cincinnati Tennis Foundation is seeking a high-energy Schools & Community Educator to lead on-site school physical education, after-school enrichment, and seasonal camp programming. This full-time, hourly role is hands-on and community-focused. You will serve as the lead face of CTF across local schools, introductory youth programs, and summer camps, ensuring youth receive top-tier physical education and social-emotional growth. Additionally, you will support impact tracking and community events, playing a pivotal role in expanding CTF's reach to youth across Greater Cincinnati.Primary ResponsibilitiesOn-Site Program Delivery (85%): Lead school PE sessions, LEAP after-school initiatives, weekend introductory programs (tennis, leagues, pickleball), and summer camp operations.Camp & Staff Supervision: Oversee daily summer camp logistics, ensuring safety, academic enrichment, and high-quality instruction while guiding seasonal staff.Community Outreach: Represent CTF at local school events, festivals, and library days to connect with local families and elevate program visibility.Data & Impact Tracking (15%): Administer year-round Hello Insight evaluations, collect program survey data, and track participant conversions alongside leadership.Partner Relations: Maintain strong relationships with school administrators, teachers, and parents to deliver a seamless partner experience.Work BreakdownProgram Delivery & Site Coordination: ~34 hours/weekImpact Tracking, Admin & Meetings: ~6 hours/weekKey QualificationsDirect experience working with youth in school, camp, or recreational sports settings.Strong organizational, group management, and leadership skills.Passion for creating inclusive, positive, and impactful experiences for young people.Familiarity with tennis, physical education, or youth sports is a plus but not a requirement.Comfort managing basic data collection systems (training provided).Benefits & PerksGroup health and prescription coverage, with access to dental, vision, and retirement options.Complimentary club membership with program discounts.

jobs.title: Sign Language Staff Interpreter at VersAbility Resources
jobs.description: Employer: VersAbility Resources Expires: 10/14/2026 About VersAbility ResourcesVersAbility Resources is a nonprofit organization based in Hampton, Virginia, dedicated to empowering people of all abilities to thrive. For more than 70 years, we have provided innovative employment, workforce development, residential, community living, and business services that promote independence, inclusion, and opportunity.Our team is passionate about making a meaningful impact by helping individuals achieve their personal and professional goals while delivering high-quality services to our community, business partners, and government customers. At VersAbility, you'll join a mission-driven organization where your work changes lives and contributes to stronger, more inclusive communities.Role OverviewThis is more than a new position—it is an important investment in communication access and inclusion at VersAbility Resources. VersAbility Resources is excited to welcome our first Sign Language Staff Interpreter, a permanent role dedicated to strengthening communication access for our Deaf and hard-of-hearing employees across the organization.Rather than relying solely on interpreting support for individual meetings or events, this position creates consistent, ongoing access to a professional who understands our employees, our workplaces, and the environments in which our teams work. For our Deaf and hard-of-hearing employees, that means greater continuity and access during orientations, training, meetings, workplace conversations, and other important moments throughout their employment experience.The Sign Language Staff Interpreter will provide professional American Sign Language (ASL)/English interpreting services across VersAbility locations, including Government Contract sites throughout Hampton Roads, while also providing virtual support to employees at geographically dispersed locations such as San Diego and Hawaii. This individual will help facilitate accurate, effective, and culturally responsive communication while respecting each employee's autonomy, communication preferences, confidentiality, and individual needs.If you are an experienced interpreter who believes communication access is essential to an inclusive workplace and wants the opportunity to become a trusted, consistent part of an organization rather than moving from assignment to assignment, this is an opportunity to make a lasting impact.What You'll DoProvide accurate, real-time, two-way interpretation between spoken English and ASL.Interpret workplace conversations, meetings, orientations, training, administrative discussions, healthcare-related interactions, technical information, and other organizational communications.Convey the complete meaning, intent, tone, context, and emotional nuance of communication rather than relying on word-for-word interpretation.Adapt interpreting approaches based on individual communication preferences, language proficiency, cultural considerations, and assignment needs.Provide interpreting support for regularly scheduled New Employee Orientation (NEO) and other organizational meetings, training, and events.Travel to VersAbility locations and Government Contract sites throughout Hampton Roads to provide on-site interpreting support.Provide virtual interpreting services for geographically dispersed VersAbility locations, including locations such as Hawaii and San Diego.Prepare for assignments by reviewing materials and becoming familiar with relevant terminology, acronyms, technical information, and subject matter.Collaborate with Deaf interpreters and other hearing interpreters during team-interpreting assignments.Coordinate appropriately with employees, managers, Human Resources, Supported Employment staff, and other stakeholders to support successful interpreting assignments.Maintain confidentiality, impartiality, professional boundaries, and ethical standards consistent with applicable professional interpreting standards, including the RID Code of Professional Conduct.Maintain required schedules, records, certifications, credentials, security clearances, and professional qualifications.Participate in continuing education, professional development, meetings, and required training.Perform other related duties as assigned.QualificationsRequiredHigh school diploma or GED equivalent.Minimum of one (1) year of professional ASL/English interpreting experience.Virginia Quality Assurance Screening (VQAS) Level III or above.Advanced proficiency in American Sign Language and spoken English.Strong understanding of Deaf culture, hearing culture, cultural norms, communication preferences, and culturally responsive interpreting practices.Knowledge of professional interpreting ethics, confidentiality, impartiality, professional boundaries, and the RID Code of Professional Conduct.Valid state-issued driver's license with an acceptable driving record.Ability and willingness to travel regularly between VersAbility locations and assigned Government Contract sites throughout Hampton Roads.REAL ID-compliant identification or valid U.S. Passport, or ability to obtain the required identification before the start date, for applicable military installation access.Ability to obtain and maintain required military installation/base access credentials and authorizations.Ability to obtain and maintain a Secret security clearance when required for an assigned Government Contract location.Ability to use Microsoft Office, Outlook, Teams, virtual meeting platforms, cameras, headsets, and other technology necessary for remote interpreting.PreferredBachelor's degree in American Sign Language/English Interpretation, Interpreter Education, ASL Studies, or a related field.Two to three years of professional interpreting experience.National Interpreter Certification (NIC).Experience interpreting in employment, government, healthcare, educational, technical, or other professional environments.ScheduleThis is a full-time, permanent position working 40 hours per week. Monday–Friday | 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m. Because interpreting needs occur across different VersAbility programs, locations, and time zones, candidates must be flexible to adjust their schedule based on employee communication needs, interpreting assignments, orientations, meetings, training, organizational events, and operational requirements. Regular local travel throughout Hampton Roads is required. The position will also provide virtual interpreting support for geographically dispersed VersAbility locations, including locations such as San Diego and Hawaii.Work Environment & Physical RequirementsThis is a dynamic interpreting position rather than a role based in one work environment. Assignments may take place in professional offices, orientation and training environments, VersAbility facilities, community locations, Government Contract sites, military installations, and virtual environments.Depending on the assignment, work environments may include changing lighting, varying temperatures, moderate to loud noise, distractions, outdoor conditions, or industrial and operational settings. Some assignments may involve lengthy, complex, technical, sensitive, or emotionally demanding communication.The position requires sustained concentration and visual attention, continuous and repetitive use of the hands, fingers, wrists, arms, and shoulders for ASL, and the upper-body stamina necessary for extended interpreting assignments. Regular travel between work locations and frequent entry and exit from a vehicle are also required.Candidates must be able to perform the essential duties and physical requirements of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation. VersAbility Resources provides reasonable accommodations in accordance with applicable law.Why Join Us?Help build something new. You will step into a newly created permanent role and help strengthen how VersAbility provides consistent communication access across the organization.Make an impact employees can experience every day. Your work will help Deaf and hard-of-hearing employees more fully access workplace communication, training, meetings, resources, and opportunities.Build continuity and trust. As a staff interpreter, you will have the opportunity to become familiar with our employees, terminology, teams, and work environments—supporting more consistent communication over time.Experience variety in your work. Assignments may take you from orientations and employee meetings to Government Contract environments, training sessions, virtual meetings, and other workplace settings.Use your profession to advance inclusion. Your expertise will directly support VersAbility's commitment to creating workplaces where employees of all abilities have meaningful access and opportunities to thrive.Grow with the role. As a new position within VersAbility, you will have the opportunity to help establish strong practices and contribute your professional perspective as our interpreting needs evolve.How to ApplyApply online through VersAbility Resources' careers site. If you need assistance or reasonable accommodation during the application process, please contact us at wehire@versability.org.Equal Opportunity EmployerVersAbility Resources is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to providing fair and equitable employment opportunities. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. We value diversity and encourage applicants of all backgrounds to apply. Certain positions are performed under the federal AbilityOne Program and are subject to applicable contractual and program requirements.

Expires: 10/14/2026 Sign-On Bonus: $4000 Retention Bonus: $1000 Summary/objective Under the supervision of the Crisis Integrated Services Coordinator, the Engagement Specialist plays a crucial role in coordinating care and providing support to children and youth experiencing crises. This position is responsible for conducting outreach and follow-up to children and families who have engaged with crisis services, with a particular focus on those who decline or disengage. The role includes delivering evidence-based Caring Contacts, reconnecting former clients, coordinating care, and fostering engagement through compassionate, proactive communication. The ideal candidate will have experience working in crisis management, case management, or child/youth services, and will be adept at collaborating with multidisciplinary teams to deliver comprehensive support to at-risk youth in Delaware. Essential functions: Caring Contacts and Crisis Reconnects Implement the Caring Contacts protocol through phone calls, mailers, and electronic communication, based on an evidence-based model designed to reduce suicide risk.Make supportive outreach to discharged clients at designated intervals post-treatment. Client Engagement and Follow-Up Conduct outreach to children and families who decline or disengage from crisis services to encourage participation and offer support.Maintain contact with former clients and families to assess ongoing needs and provide appropriate referrals or follow-up.Serve as a point of contact for post-discharge engagement, ensuring continuity of care and supporting client wellness.System Engagement and Resource Coordination Collaborate with internal and external service providers to support client care plan, ensuring that all immediate and ongoing needs are addressed holistic support.Documentation and Reporting: Maintain accurate and up-to-date records of all client interactions and collateral follow-ups in accordance with program policies and state regulations.Prepare and submit regular case updates and reports, including documentation of progress, barriers, and recommendations for further intervention or resources.Competencies/ Capabilities: Crisis Management: Ability to effectively assess and manage urgent, high-stress situations while providing emotional support and practical solutions.Collaboration: Strong teamwork and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work with diverse stakeholders.Problem Solving: Capacity to think critically and find solutions quickly in complex, time-sensitive situations.Communication: Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to clearly explain complex information.Empathy and Compassion: A compassionate approach to working with children and families in crisis, with an understanding of trauma and mental health issues.Cultural Competency: Understanding and respecting the diversity of youth and families served, and providing services in a culturally sensitive manner.Supervisory responsibilities: none Work environment: Office based, Partial telecommuting with approval Physical demands: Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computerMay be regulations, and community resources for children and families.Preferred qualifications: Advanced degree in a related fieldExperience working in a 24/7 crisis response programBilingual About Delaware Guidance ServicesDGS is the largest non-profit provider of outpatient behavioral health services for children and families in Delaware, and the only statewide organization of its kind continuously accredited by The Joint Commission since 1999. Each year, DGS serves an average of 3,500 children and youth through a clinically excellent continuum of care that includes outpatient therapy, community‑based services, school‑based supports, mobile crisis response, and short‑term youth crisis stabilization. We are passionate about what we do and dream of inspiring community through our commitment and mission. We are a welcoming agency that believes that ALL people from the newborn to the elderly are valued members of our communities. If you want to make a difference where you live while serving alongside other amazing professionals, Lutheran Family Services Rocky Mountains invites you to apply.DEPARTMENT OVERVIEWThe Refugee & Asylee programs at LFSRM help people uprooted by persecution and violence work towards self-sufficiency through essential resettlement services including case management, employment, housing, school registration, cultural orientation, and referrals to internal and external services for English language acquisition, health and mental health needs, employment, and economic development. Services are delivered in a culturally responsive manner and often in another language.REQUIRED COMPETENCIESOccupational CompetenciesProvide case management: Familiarity with assessment, care planning, facilitation, coordination, and advocacy for support on behalf of and in collaboration with individuals or families.Coordinate services: Knowledge of currently available community resources, services, and supports, and ability to connect individuals or families to appropriate resources to meet their needs through referral, application, or enrollment assistance.Deliver services within diverse cultural communities: Skills and sensitivity in working with individuals and families from a variety of ethnic and cultural backgrounds.Apply Person-Centered Care: Treats individuals as partners in planning, developing and accessing care to ensure services are appropriate to their needs. regulations and guidance, and contractual requirements.Provide crisis intervention: Experience with crisis management, problem solving, and mediation best practices.Communicate professionally: Ability to communicate professionally and cooperate with colleagues, other professionals, community partners, and other individuals involved in the care and coordination of services.Manage case file compliance: Maintain organized, up-to-date physical case files and digital records in accordance with program, agency, and funder requirements.Ensure data accuracy and integrity: Consistently enter, update, and review client data in online systems to ensure records are complete, accurate, and audit ready.Meet documentation timelines: Complete all required documentation within established deadlines, balancing client services with timely data entry, quality and attention to detail.Foundational CompetenciesActive Listening: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.Social Perceptiveness: Being aware of others' reactions and attempting to understand the personal and cultural reasons for their reactions.Complex Problem Solving: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.Critical Thinking: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.EXAMPLE ACTIVITIESCoordinates with an advocate and resource for clients and provides equal treatment to all client groups in accordance with the agency's commitment to the dignity of all persons.Works collaboratively with other members jobs.title: Behavioral Support & Career Technician at Exceptional Minds
jobs.description: Employer: Exceptional Minds Expires: 10/14/2026 For over a decade, our award-winning nonprofit academy and working production studio has been preparing young adults on the autism spectrum for careers in animation and the digital arts. Exceptional-Minds develops a diverse and inclusive workforce of thoughtful and talented artists once on the margins, who now have what every young professional seeks - dignity, hope, and a command of the skills and tools necessary to lead successful careers.Title: Behavioral Support & Career TechnicianFLSA Classification: NonexemptJob Type: Part TimeDepartment: Studio/Administration This is a part time role up to 20 hours per week. All work will be performed in-person at one office location, under the supervision of the Behavior Analyst and Studio Director. JOB DESCRIPTION Summary/ObjectiveDrawing on prior experience and RBT certification, the Behavioral Support & Career Technician at Exceptional Minds plays a key role in fostering behavioral wellness and a supportive studio/workplace environment for Artists. The ideal candidate will observe workplace dynamics, facilitate behavioral support and skills training, and provide guidance to Artists navigating social and/or behavioral challenges. Working under the supervision of a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) and the Director of Studio Programs, the Behavioral Support & Career Technician will collaborate closely with staff to help cultivate a positive, inclusive, and effective studio environment aligned with Exceptional-Minds’ mission and values.Impact of the RoleThe Behavioral Support & Career Technician advances the Exceptional Minds mission by providing the behavioral and wellness support that allows Artists to engage fully in their career development. Through individualized support, proactive wellness programming, and cross-team collaboration, this role helps ensure EM Artists have the stability and resources needed to growin their talent and advocate for themselves in the creative industry. Essential Functions● Support Artists in further developing vocational readiness skills throughout their employment at EM.● Meet with Artists and support staff to note potential contingencies that are impacting performance or comfort (i.e., ABC data collection).● Collect data using provided templates and transfer data to appropriate spreadsheets for graphing.● Monitor workspaces as arranged by the Behavior Analyst/Studio Director and follow protocols for ensuring all data collection remains private and confidential.● Provide on-call support with de-escalation when distress responses are reported.● Assist with creating training material to share important behavioral insights with staff.● Collaborate with the BCBA to review feedback for behavioral plans, and review modifications or accommodations in weekly/biweekly meetings.● Abide by HIPAA and relevant BACB ethical guidelines when communicating client information orally and in writing.● Coach Artists on self-advocacy and professionalism as they prepare to enter the digital arts industry.● Assist Artists with documenting accomplishments and progress using established tracking tools.● Communicate observations regarding Artist progress to the BCBA and Studio staff as appropriate.Required Experience & Qualifications:● Active Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) certification through the BACB.● Bachelor’s degree in progress or completed in a related behavioral, education, or human services field (e.g., Psychology, Education, Special Education, Human Development, Social Work, Child Development, Sociology).● Basic knowledge of Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) principles.● Experience supporting autistic adults in an educational, clinical, vocational, orcommunity-based setting.● Strong communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills.● Ability to accurately collect behavioral data and maintain documentation.● Ability to work collaboratively under the supervision of the BCBA and StudioDirector. Preferred Experience & Qualifications:● Experience supporting autistic adults in employment, vocational, educational, or studio settings.● Experience collecting behavioral data (e.g., ABC data, frequency, duration,interval recording, task analysis).● Familiarity with graphing behavioral data and basic proficiency with GoogleWorkspace (Google Docs, Google Slides) and/or Microsoft Excel.● Interest in vocational readiness, workplace success, and career development for autistic adults.● Basic familiarity with workplace accommodations and ADA compliance.● Commitment to neurodiversity-affirming and trauma-informed practices.● Experience working with groups/multiple individuals simultaneously.We are an equal-opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, or national origin. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform critical job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request an accommodation.

jobs.feedName: Michael D. Eisner College of Education
jobs.title: Mitigation Specialist at State Appellate Defender Office
jobs.description: Employer: State Appellate Defender Office Expires: 10/15/2026 Join Michigan’s State Appellate Defender Office (SADO) as a full-time, limited-term Mitigation Specialist for the Private Counsel Division of SADO. The salary range for this position is $57,252 to $96,048, depending on experience. Mitigation specialists are supervised and trained by the Michigan Appellate Assigned Counsel System (MAACS) Administrator or the MAACS Roster Support and Performance Manager. This position can be based out of SADO’s Detroit or Lansing office. The position requires extensive travel (about 20% of the time) and offers a flexible hybrid work policy. Job ResponsibilitiesSpecific duties include, but are not limited to:Interview, and build rapport with incarcerated clients to learn about their background, the facts of the offense, current experiences while incarcerated, and specific needs upon release;Identify, locate, and interview family, friends, community members, and other individuals to compile material in mitigation of sentence;Travel extensively throughout Michigan and occasionally out of state to visit clients in prison and interview witnesses;Obtain, analyze, and summarize records and documents, including prison records, social files, school records, and medical and mental health records;Prepare reports, including client and witness interview memos, social history reports, and sentencing memoranda, using creative writing and storytelling techniques;Identify support for clients transitioning back into the community;Identify and consult with appropriate experts to obtain reports and prepare for hearings;Prepare clients for testifying in court or presenting allocution; In limited circumstances, testify in court;Train attorneys and staff on mitigation and parole hearings; andAssist attorneys with general hearing preparation such as preparing exhibits, coordinating with witnesses, attending court hearings, and other necessary tasks.QualificationsMitigation specialists draw from a diverse range of professional, academic, and life experiences to inform their work. Mitigation specialists must be empathetic communicators, effective interviewers, curious investigators, critical readers, data managers, creative writers, compassionate listeners, and zealous advocates. At SADO we are dedicated to building a multi-disciplinary team with diverse perspectives and experiences, so if you are excited about this role but you do not meet every qualification in this job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be the right candidate for the job.Education: Education and/or equivalent experience in social work, social sciences, psychology, forensic psychology, journalism, anthropology, criminal justice, or a related field;Commitments:Commitment to client-centered, zealous advocacy; Commitment to the inherent worth and dignity of clients;Commitment to cultural humility and cultural competency;Knowledge and Abilities:Knowledge of the criminal legal system, preferably in Michigan; Experience in investigation;Excellent communication, trauma-informed interviewing, and interpersonal skills;Understanding of mental health signs and symptoms, the effects of trauma, developmental and intellectual disabilities, and the impacts of social, cultural, historical, political, religious, racial, environmental, and ethnic influences on behavior;Ability to prioritize multiple client cases, deadlines, and demands;Ability to work flexible hours, including evenings, nights, and early mornings, and to travel throughout the state to attend hearings, meet with incarcerated clients, interview witnesses, and obtain mitigation material;Possess a valid driver’s license;Ability to organize, interpret, and synthesize large quantities of information into persuasive, compelling, and thorough written narratives;Flexible and creative thinking;The ability to work as part of the defense team under the lead of the case attorney, and maintain confidentiality;Proficiency with Microsoft Word and Outlook, Adobe Acrobat, Excel, and general office equipment;Self-motivated, with the ability to handle constructive feedback; andCandidates must be a current resident of or relocate to Michigan by hire date.To ApplySubmit a resume and a cover letter via email by October 11, 2026, to jobs@sado.org and include “MAACS Mitigation Specialist 2026-13” in the subject line. Applications without a resume and cover letter will not be considered. The cover letter should address the reasons underlying your interest in the work and explain your commitment to working with incarcerated people and people convicted of crimes.SADO is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. A felony conviction does not prohibit employment at SADO.

jobs.description: Employer: Georgetown Day School Expires: 10/15/2026 About the SchoolGeorgetown Day School opened its doors in 1945 as the first integrated school in a segregated city. GDS was founded by seven changemaker families who envisioned a school committed not only to academic excellence and educational innovation but also to respect and care for others. Believing that diversity is a critical foundation for the most transformational learning, they established a school where all children would be welcomed, celebrated, and challenged to be their best selves.Today, the School’s philosophy and programs strongly reflect its roots. GDS fosters a community of belonging while lifting up every student’s unique gifts, building in each the capacity for compassion, leadership, and creating positive change. 1125 engaged and talented PK-12 students across three divisions love to learn and learn to change the world in GDS’s exciting urban campus with its outstanding facilities. Recognized as one the most dynamic educational institutions in our capital city and nation, GDS today is in a uniquely attractive position, with a deeply-felt and lived history, clear mission, and genuine openness to the possibilities that lie ahead. Georgetown Day School’s (GDS) Office of Auxiliary Programs seeks staff to become part of its department (extended day programs) for the 2026-2027 school year.GDS Auxiliary Programs Mission:While participating in GDS Auxiliary Programs, children will explore, learn, and create through hands-on and interpersonal inquiry, gaining an appreciation for themselves, others, and the world. GDS Auxiliary Programs Team Members teach new skills and provide tools that enable children to develop into great people who strive to learn, understand, try new things, and care for others. Position Description:GDS seeks to hire several School Year Auxiliary Programs Team Members to support ongoing school year programming. We seek individuals with experience working with elementary and middle school-aged children (ages 4–13) who are prepared to challenge students academically, physically, and artistically and to establish authentic relationships with the children in the extended-day program. The ability to provide rich, mission-aligned, and creative content, to develop authentic relationships, to work collaboratively with colleagues, and to place children’s interests and experiences at the heart of the classroom are essential components of the job. Location: On-campus at 4200 Davenport Street NW, Washington, DC, 20016Start Date: Immediate start (once cleared to work)Type of Opportunity: Part-timeFLSA Status: Non-exempt Compensation: $21.32 to 31.90/hour, depending on years of experience (compensation for students starts at minimum wage)Note: Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.Potential Hours and Work Functions:Extended Day (M/T/W/H/F - 2:30 - 6:30 p.m.)Early Morning Grasshopper (M/T/W/H/F - 7:00 - 8:00 am)Break Camp (Various days throughout the school year - 8:00 a.m. - 4:00 p.m.)Staff Childcare (Various days throughout the school year - 8:00 a.m. - 4:00 p.m.)External Relations (Various evenings and weekends - various times)These team members may plan weekly special activities to pique our students’ interests in a variety of ways. jobs.feedName: Michael D. Eisner College of Education
jobs.title: Literacy Leader at St Nicks Alliance
jobs.description: Employer: St Nicks Alliance Expires: 10/15/2026 Literacy Leader (Part-Time, After-School)St. Nicks Alliance | North Brooklyn | Fall 2026Pay: $20.85/hourHours: Approximately 20 hours per week during the school yearSchedule: Weekday afternoons, roughly 2:00–6:00pm, plus one morning per week for professional developmentLocation: North Brooklyn — Williamsburg, Greenpoint, Bushwick, and Bed-Stuy school sitesHelp kids fall in love with reading.St. Nicks Alliance is looking for Literacy Leaders to lead after-school literacy programming at our elementary and middle school sites across North Brooklyn.You don't need a teaching certificate. You need experience leading groups of kids, genuine interest in literacy and youth development, and the willingness to be coached. We provide the curriculum, weekly professional development, and one-on-one instructional coaching — your job is to bring it to life for students.This is a good fit if you're a college student or recent graduate in education, English, or psychology; a paraprofessional or teaching assistant looking for additional hours; a teaching artist; or someone considering a career in education who wants real classroom experience with real support behind it.About St. Nicks AllianceSt. Nicks Alliance is a North Brooklyn community organization working to transform the lives of low- and moderate-income people through employment, education, housing, elder care, and social services. Our after-school programs serve children across North Brooklyn with literacy, arts, homework help, and social-emotional learning.What you'll doInstruction. Lead twice-weekly literacy lessons for groups of 10–20 elementary or middle school students using our internally developed curriculum. Provide targeted small-group and individual instruction incorporating Science of Reading elements and the day school's literacy techniques. Build lessons that draw on students' home culture, values, interests, and language.Assessment. Assess student work formally and informally to determine growth and next steps. Document learning through notes, work collection, and photos. Collect literacy outcome and attitudinal data for our School Success Model research program. Keep site directors and group leaders informed about each student's strengths and challenges.Professional development and coaching. Participate in mandatory weekly professional development and in regular coaching sessions with our Instructional Coach or Associate Director of Education. Give feedback to our curriculum writers on what's working and what isn't — Literacy Leaders genuinely shape the curriculum here.Collaboration. Work with the school's literacy team to align our curriculum with school goals. Coordinate with the BK Story Voyager coordinator on book selection and programming. Partner with reading specialists, tutors, teaching artists, and the school's SEL transformational coach.Safety and supervision. Follow DOHMH, OCFS, and CDC safety protocols. Stay actively engaged in supervising students across all program components — meals, transitions, outdoor play, field trips, arrival, and dismissal.What we're looking forAt least two years leading lessons or structured activities for groups of ten or more childrenCompetency in lesson leadership — effective transitions, student engagement, clear directionsAbility to build productive relationships with students while maintaining appropriate adult-child boundariesStrong self-awareness and interest in or experience with Social Emotional LearningPrior professional development in literacy, youth development, or teachingExceptional communication skills for working with leadership, program directors, colleagues, students, parents, and school facultyUnderstanding of the strengths and challenges of our students, including familiarity with their neighborhoods, cultures, languages, and valuesCapacity to adapt in dynamic after-school environmentsHelpful but not required: experience teaching project- or theme-based lessons; experience writing lesson plans with learning objectives; interest in advancing professionally in education, literacy, or child development.Why this job is worth havingMost part-time youth jobs hand you a room and wish you luck. This one comes with a written curriculum, weekly paid professional development, and an instructional coach whose job is helping you get better. People who want to teach use this role to find out whether they actually do — and to build the skills before they commit to a credential program.How to applySend a resume and a cover letter explaining why you are the right person for this role at St. Nicks Alliance to Tim Fredrick at tfredrick@stnicksalliance.org, with "Literacy Leader" in the subject line. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.St. Nicks Alliance is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to building a staff that reflects the communities we serve, and we encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds.

jobs.description: Employer: Berkshire Farm Center and Services For Youth Expires: 10/15/2026 The Community Care Specialist provides intensive interaction and support to youth and families in need of extra assistance on a one-to-one basis through recreational, educational, cultural and social activities. The position is responsible for assisting the team with supervising, counseling, teaching and supporting children, families and foster families as needed. The Family Visitation and Empowerment Program (FVEP) is a trauma-informed reunification program dedicated to maintaining and strengthening family connections for children in foster care and other court-ordered placements. jobs.feedName: Michael D. Eisner College of Education
jobs.title: Lead Teacher, Early Childhood at Big Dreams Child Care
jobs.description: Employer: Big Dreams Child Care Expires: 10/15/2026 OverviewBig Dreams Child Care is a licensed early childhood education center serving families in southern Brooklyn from our Avenue U location. Our program spans infants through Pre-K, and we are building a teaching team defined by professionalism, consistency, and high expectations for both children and adults.We are hiring Lead Teachers who are able to effectively lead a classroom and be held to a professional standard. The role carries real responsibility: you set the tone for your room, lead the assistant teachers assigned to it, and serve as a point contact for the families in your care. In return, you will work within a transparent environment, receive direct support from our Educational Director focused on classroom quality, and have a defined path for advancement within the organization.This position is based exclusively at our Avenue U center.Job DescriptionThe Lead Teacher is responsible for the safety, development, and daily experience of every child in the assigned classroom; the quality and consistency of the educational program; full compliance with NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene Article 47 regulations; the relationship with each enrolled family; and the direction and performance of the Assistant Teachers assigned to the room. This is a non-exempt, full-time position reporting to the Educational Director.ResponsibilitiesClassroom leadership and instructionPlan and deliver a developmentally appropriate daily program for the assigned age group, aligned to the center's curriculum framework, with structured routines, small-group instruction, and purposeful playEstablish and maintain classroom routines, transitions, and behavior expectations that create a calm, predictable environment for childrenDifferentiate instruction and care to meet the individual needs of each child, including children with developmental or behavioral support needsHealth, safety, and complianceMaintain required staff-to-child ratios at all times and manage coverage transitions with the Educational DirectorComplete daily attendance, health checks, incident reports, and all required documentation accurately and on the same dayKeep the classroom inspection-ready under Article 47 standards, including health, hygiene, allergy, and safe-sleep protocols where applicableServe as a mandated reporter and follow all center policies regarding child protectionAssessment and family engagementConduct ongoing developmental observations and complete periodic assessments for each child as directedCommunicate with families daily through Brightwheel and in person at drop-off and pick-upRespond to family questions and concerns the same day, and escalate to the Educational Director when appropriateRepresent the center professionally in every family interactionTeam leadershipDirect the daily work of one to three Assistant Teachers: assign responsibilities, model expectations, and provide real-time feedbackContribute to the performance evaluations of assigned Assistant TeachersEnsure the classroom operates to standard during your planning time, breaks, and absences by preparing your team accordinglyProfessional conductMaintain reliable, punctual attendance in accordance with the center's attendance and call-out policy. Children and colleagues depend on your presence, and this expectation is fundamental to the role.Participate in staff meetings, required training hours, and scheduled performance reviewsAdhere to the employee handbook and all center policiesQualificationsRequiredNYC Article 47 group teacher qualified: NYS Early Childhood (Birth to Grade 2) certification, or a bachelor's or associate degree in early childhood education or a related field with an approved study plan toward certificationMinimum of one year of experience as the lead teacher of a classroom in a licensed early childhood programAbility to obtain and maintain all NYC DOHMH clearances, including fingerprinting, Statewide Central Register (SCR) clearance, medical clearance and immunizations, CPR and First Aid certification, and mandated reporter trainingStrong written and verbal communication skills in EnglishProficiency with classroom management technology (Brightwheel or comparable platform)Physical ability to lift up to 40 pounds, sit on the floor, stand for extended periods, and respond quickly to children's needsPreferredTwo or more years of lead classroom experienceNYS Early Childhood certification or a master's degree in early childhood educationExperience with infant or toddler classroomsBilingual proficiency (Russian, Spanish, Mandarin, or Hebrew)Performance standards. Lead Teachers are evaluated each September and January. Results determine placement within the pay scale and eligibility for advancement. New hires complete a 90-day introductory period with structured check-ins at 30, 60, and 90 days.Our standard. We hold Lead Teachers to the highest standard of professionalism in early childhood education, and we are deliberate about who we hire. A Lead Teacher at Big Dreams is a model of our mission and vision, in and out of the classroom: in how you prepare, how you speak to children, how you lead your team, how you present yourself to families, and how reliably you show up. Families entrust us with their children on the strength of the people we put in front of them, and every Lead Teacher is expected to be worthy of that trust every day. We look for teachers who take ownership without being asked, hold themselves accountable before anyone else has to, treat the standard as a source of pride rather than a burden, and raise the level of the people around them. If that describes how you work, you will find a center that backs you, invests in you, and rewards you for it.Big Dreams Child Care is an equal opportunity employer. All employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.
